Subject: QueryLayr + Redwood tracing SDK: pilot ask

Hi Priyom —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. QueryLayr is built on top of LangChain (we use the Python runtime) and we want to instrument end-to-end traces for generation requests so we can measure latency breakdowns and attribution across our prompt pipeline. The goal for the pilot is simple: validate Redwood's tracing SDK integration with our LangChain flows, confirm LlamaIndex connector compatibility for indexing-derived context, and gather token-level latency stats for a 2-week sandbox.

Can we start with a short checklist:
- Sandbox credentials (API key, region)
- Recommended SDK version and any Redwood trace spec docs
- Any quickstart or sample LangChain app you recommend we run in our staging environment

I can loop in our eng lead if useful — copying our integrations alias. Would prefer to kick off next week if that lines up.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Brown
Head of Integrations, SynthesisWorks

Hi Aisha —

Excited to run this pilot with SynthesisWorks. High level we can support both LangChain and LlamaIndex instrumentation; our Python tracing SDK supports automatic spans for request lifecycle and explicit spans you can attach around prompt construction or index lookups. Quick answers to your checklist:

- Sandbox: I'll provision a scoped sandbox API key (region: us-west-2) and post credentials to the Drive folder with limited access.
- SDK: start with redwood-trace-python v0.9.x for the LangChain adapter (we have minor breaking changes in v1.0 planned, so 0.9.x is our stable pilot branch).
- Quickstart: I'll attach a tiny sample app that exercises a LangChain Chain -> LlamaIndex query -> generate path. It includes a README to show where to drop the API key and how to enable verbose tracing.

Two clarifying questions:
1) Do you use streaming generation in QueryLayr (we instrument streams differently to capture per-chunk latencies)?
2) Any data residency or redaction rules we should apply in the sandbox traces?

Action plan proposal (pilot scope):
- Week 0: credential exchange, sample app run, baseline metrics capture
- Week 1: instrumented integration with 2 sample LLM prompts and LlamaIndex context lookups
- Week 2: collect telemetry, validate token-level latency and attribution, joint review call

If that works I'll create a short SOW and loop partner ops. Kimberly — can you own an acceptance test checklist for SDK compatibility? Vanessa — I'll need a short SOW/pilot commercial note.

Cheers,
Priyom

Thanks Priyom / Vanessa —

SOW looks good from our side. A few answers to your clarifying questions:
- Streaming: yes, QueryLayr exposes streaming by default for long responses; we'd like to capture per-chunk latencies so we can attribute slowdowns to model vs infra vs prompt formatting.
- Data residency: for the pilot we can use the Redwood sandbox in us-west-2 and there is no extra PII we need redacted in traces.

I've uploaded a small sample repo with a minimal LangChain + LlamaIndex app that reproduces our production chain: QueryLayr uses LangChain 0.1.23 and LlamaIndex 0.5.8 (we're on those pinned versions). The attachment contains the app and a small dataset.

Attachment: querylayr-sample-app.zip (archive/zip)

Code note (snippet):

# LangChain chain snippet (simplified)
from redwood_trace import RedwoodTracer
tracer = RedwoodTracer(api_key="REDACTED")

with tracer.span("querylayr.chain"):
    prompt = build_prompt(context, user_query)
    with tracer.span("llamaindex.lookup"):
        context_block = index.query(user_query)
    with tracer.span("llm.generate"):
        result = llm.generate(prompt, stream=True)

Please confirm the recommended SDK flags for stream instrumentation — happy to get the walkthrough scheduled next Tuesday.

— Aisha

Aisha —

Great, thanks for the sample app and version pins. Confirming the plan and next actions: 

Action items (owners):
- Priyom: provision sandbox API key (scoped) and upload to Drive.
- Kimberly: publish compatibility acceptance checklist for LangChain 0.1.23 and LlamaIndex 0.5.8, run the sample app and report any adapter gaps.
- Marissa: create a short integration guide for partners (how to toggle stream instrumentation flags and where to find token-level latency in Console).
- Aisha / SynthesisWorks: run the sample app in your staging with the provided sandbox key and share first dataset traces (we'll keep them in the sandbox retention window).

Quick answers on stream instrumentation:
- Use redwood-trace-python v0.9.x with tracer.enable_stream_spans=True. That creates per-chunk spans named llm.stream.chunk and captures chunk-size + elapsed_ms attributes.
- For LlamaIndex lookups we recommend wrapping index.query in explicit spans as you already do; we will collect both server-side generation spans and client-side index spans and correlate by request id.

I've created the HubSpot deal and linked the Drive folder here: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567/SW-7892 and uploaded the SOW draft to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_onboarding

Thanks — looking forward to this pilot.

Priyom
